content:
maya: Noticed a reproducible oddity when onboarding aurora-lite-v2 (q5): vertical Cantonese subtitles that include an inline Arabic greeting sometimes end up with timestamps reversed in the final output. Minimal repro attached. looping in @kenji @li-wei for triage.

kenji: can you paste the raw input and what fp16 vs q5 return? curious if this is tokenization, beam search, or postprocess.

maya: raw snippet we used:
```


張小姐：‎السلام  
(下一行) 09:45
```
(I scrubbed some markup; main point is vertical layout + Arabic phrase + short timestamp)

fp16 output:
```
張小姐：السلام عليكم
(下一行) 09:45
```
q5 output (beam=5):
```
張小姐：السلام عليكم
(下一行) 54:90  <-- numerics flipped/garbled
```
q5 greedy (beam=1) matches fp16 (09:45).

li-wei: please dump tokenizer tokens and beam hypotheses. token ids equal? sometimes Kernels can return same token ids but re-ranker picks different beam.

maya: tokens look identical between runtimes, posted below (ids shortened):
```
# tokens fp16: [100, 204, 333, 777, 888, 999]
# tokens q5:  [100, 204, 333, 777, 888, 999]
```
but beam final strings differ as above.

dmitri: suggests scoring differences post-quantization. Do we apply any locale-specific normalization in the detokenizer for vertical layout? also check bidi markers around Arabic.

maya: we add a vertical-layout hook that preserves fullwidth punctuation, but turning that off doesn't change the failure. bidi markers () are present around the Arabic phrase in the input.

sam: tie-breaker / score binning hypothesis: if q5 logprobs are quantized to fewer buckets, two hypotheses can end up extremely close and tiebreak logic might prefer a shorter or lexical-later one. have we changed tie-breaker recently? @ci-bot can you show recent runtime changes touching beam tie policy?

ci-bot: recent commits: runtime PR #1219 updated beam tie resolution to favor path with lower memory copy overhead (perf optimization). No locale-specific changes.

li-wei: can we compare beam scores for the top candidates (fp16 vs q5) and the token sequences around numerics?

maya: pasted beam top2 snapshots:
```
# fp16 top2:
H1 -12.102233 (.... 09 : 45)
H2 -12.152999 (.... 90 : 54)
# q5 top2:
H1 -12.120000 (.... 90 : 54)
H2 -12.119999 (.... 09 : 45)  <-- inversion
```
So q5 has tiny inversion.

kenji: ok that points to quant-induced rounding. quickest mitigation: implement deterministic lexicographic tie-breaker for numeric token sequences (hotfix) and add a jitter based on higher precision run to the scoring when two quantized scores are within epsilon. I'll pick up the tie-breaker.

dmitri: also add a regression test into the subtitle qual harness that covers vertical CJK + embedded RTL script + timestamp. Mark as must-pass for q5 rollout.

sam: created an internal ticket for product: SUBS-APAC-54 to flag customer-facing risk. not a widespread failure but high annoyance for subtitles.

maya: I put a failing example into the onboarding bucket and created an evaluation notebook entry. PR link: https://git.redwood/aurora/onboard/PR-88 (internal).

ci-bot: summary metrics: on small vertical-subset (N=8.2k), q5 shows a -0.5 BLEU and +0.9 TER concentrated on timestamp-like tokens.

li-wei: plan for bisect: check runtime tie-breaker change PRs (#1219) and the q5 quant packing rule change in the kernel team. I can run a binary bisect on q5 pack releases to isolate the change.

kenji: I'll re-run the sample on dedicated (node-delta) with float-emulation turned on for q5 (flag --float-emulate) to see if rounding explains it. if float-emulate matches fp16, kernel rounding is culprit.

maya: flags used in failing run: --deterministic True --seed 7 --beam_size 5 --locale vertical_zh_hk --length_penalty 0.8 --float-emulate False.

dmitri: note: ensure deterministic GPU kernel paths used, some CUDA kernels can be nondet across runs; confirm cudnn deterministic flags.

kenji: rerun queued. will report back. :hourglass: 

maya: thx. tagging RU and HK folks for visibility. will update the qual notebook when we get a fix. :pushpin:
